chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from a man, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Sunnah dowry, how it became five hundred. He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, obligated upon Himself that if a believer glorifies Him (Allahu Akbar) one hundred times, glorifies Him (SubhanAllah) one hundred times, praises Him (Alhamdulillah) one hundred times, proclaims His Oneness (La ilaha illallah) one hundred times, and sends blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny one hundred times, then says, 'O Allah, marry me to the Houris with large beautiful eyes,' Allah will marry him to Hawra' (a specific Houri) and make that (recitation) her dowry.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that the Sunnah dowry of the believing women is five hundred dirhams. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did that.

And any believer who proposes to his brother for his honorable daughter and states the dowry as five hundred dirhams, but he does not marry her to him, has been disloyal to him, and deserves from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He does not marry him to a Houri.

key_terms.حَوْرَاءَ عَيْنٍ: Hawra' with large beautiful eyes (a specific Houri)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual origin and legal ruling of the Sunnah dowry in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith links the legal standard of the Sunnah dowry (500 dirhams) to a spiritual precedent where Allah obligated Himself to grant a believer who performs specific dhikr and salawat one hundred times each, and asks for marriage to the Houris, a spouse from the Houris, with the spiritual reward serving as her dowry. This spiritual precedent was then revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as the legal standard for the dowry of believing women. The narration further establishes that if a believer proposes marriage to another believer's sister and is refused without valid reason, he is considered 'blocked' (mu'qad) and forfeits the reward of marrying a Houri, highlighting the social and spiritual weight of the dowry agreement.
